title: PiPi — Chatbot at Bamnang
subtitle: A multilingual chatbot helping students discover universities, scholarships, and mentors in one conversation.
description: Bringing Bamnang's educational resources together so students can ask questions naturally in English, Khmer, or Khmer Latin.
appPrompt: Experience PiPi firsthand by downloading and testing the Bamnang App.

images.title: Campus & Major Discovery
images.caption: Exploring universities, faculties, and admission details via conversation

images.title: Mentor Consultation
images.caption: Inquiring about mentors, guidance, and scheduled study sessions

images.title: Scholarship Search
images.caption: Discovering active scholarships, eligibility, and application deadlines

situation.title: The Situation
situation.paragraph: Bamnang offers helpful information about universities, majors, scholarships, events, and mentors, but this knowledge was scattered across different places. At the same time, students communicate in different ways—some type in English, some in Khmer script, and many in Khmer Latin. This made it difficult for students to find clear answers quickly through a single conversation.

task.title: The Task
task.paragraph: The goal was to make PiPi understand and respond accurately across English, Khmer, and Khmer Latin, while uniting all Bamnang knowledge into one seamless chat experience that feels simple, natural, and helpful for any student.

action.title: The Action
action.paragraph: I organized knowledge from multiple Bamnang sources and designed the conversation flow to handle mixed-language inputs smoothly. By testing real student queries and everyday phrasing, I refined the responses to ensure answers were direct, easy to understand, and focused on what students actually need.
points: Conducted technical research to evaluate LLM frameworks, agent architectures, and tools suitable for Bamnang’s chatbot.
Designed the multi-agent chatbot architecture and defined how different agents should handle different student needs.
Organized and structured knowledge from multiple Bamnang sources for chatbot use.
Designed the conversation flow to support different types of student questions and interactions.
Worked on multi-language support for Khmer, English, and mixed Khmer-English inputs.
Designed the database structure to support chatbot knowledge, conversations, sessions, and related data.
Tested the chatbot with real student questions and everyday phrasing to identify gaps and improve responses.
Refined prompts and chatbot logic to make answers direct, simple, and relevant.
Worked on the backend implementation end-to-end, connecting chatbot logic, knowledge sources, database, and APIs.
Iteratively improved the system based on real usage, testing, and student needs.

result.title: The Result
result.paragraph: PiPi now offers a friendly, multilingual way for students to explore educational opportunities in one place, making school and scholarship guidance accessible no matter how they choose to communicate.

title: Major-Recommendation at Bamnang (MCT)
subtitle: A guided test helping students connect their interests and strengths with suitable university majors and careers.
description: Guiding high school graduates from self-understanding to matching job clusters and university majors.
appPrompt: Experience the Major Career Test (MCT) firsthand by downloading and testing the Bamnang App.

images.title: Interactive Self-Discovery
images.caption: Guided questionnaire assessing student interests, skills, and personal strengths

images.title: Career Cluster Matching
images.caption: Connecting student characteristics with relevant professional fields and job pathways

images.title: Actionable Major Suggestions
images.caption: Clear breakdown of recommended university majors and curriculum directions

situation.title: The Situation
situation.paragraph: Many students want a good career after graduation but struggle to pick the right university major because they are unsure of their strengths, interests, and potential job paths. Bamnang needed a simple, guided tool to help students explore their options without feeling overwhelmed.

task.title: The Task
task.paragraph: The goal was to build a student-friendly assessment that turns questionnaire answers into meaningful recommendations with clear explanations, rather than just displaying raw numbers or arbitrary test scores.

action.title: The Action
action.paragraph: I designed the Major Career Test around students' real interests and traits, mapping their answers directly to relevant job clusters. I structured the results so students can step-by-step connect who they are to possible career paths and matching majors.
points: Conducted a literature review with the college to research global career clusters, workforce trends, and relevant career/education data.
Translated the research into a career-cluster framework that connects students’ interests and traits with potential career directions.
Designed the Major Career Test logic and scoring flow, including how student responses determine relevant job clusters and career paths.
Designed and developed the backend architecture end-to-end, from database structure and APIs to scoring, mapping, and result generation.
Structured the result experience so students can move step-by-step from self-understanding → job clusters → career paths → relevant university majors.
Integrated the test with the broader platform so the results can support personalized recommendations and future student guidance.

result.title: The Result
result.paragraph: Students now receive clear, personalized recommendations that explain why certain majors fit them, helping them make confident, informed decisions about their university education.

title: Chhnang Khmer — Recipe Kit Delivery Web App
subtitle: An authentic, culturally inspired e-commerce platform allowing customers to order pre-portioned Khmer recipe kits with step-by-step guides.
description: An individual capstone project at Sisters of Code promoting Cambodian culinary heritage with client-side JSON data handling, interactive cart, and responsive UX/UI.
appPrompt: Experience the live, interactive recipe kit platform hosted on GitHub Pages.
pdfSubtitle: Official Presentation Deck for Sisters of Code Capstone

images.title: Culinary Hero & Brand Identity
images.caption: Immersive landing page celebrating authentic Khmer recipes with prominent call-to-actions

images.title: Storytelling & Brand Mission
images.caption: Highlighting the mission to make cooking traditional Khmer dishes accessible with less prep time and zero food waste

images.title: Recipe Catalog & Dynamic Filtering
images.caption: Interactive multi-criteria filtering by category, cuisine, diet set, and price range

situation.title: The Situation
situation.paragraph: Many people love authentic Khmer dishes but find traditional cooking time-consuming due to sourcing and prepping ingredients. Chhnang Khmer was envisioned as a recipe kit delivery platform to make cooking heritage food at home convenient and accessible.

task.title: The Task
task.paragraph: As an individual capstone at Sisters of Code, my goal was to design and build a multi-page responsive web app using HTML5, CSS3, Bootstrap 5, and pure JavaScript with zero backend dependencies.
points: Craft a culturally inspired UI/UX design with custom typography and color tokens.
Implement dynamic client-side filtering, recipe details, cart handling, and order tracking.
Manage application state and mock catalog data using JSON and localStorage.

action.title: The Action
action.paragraph: I developed the frontend architecture end-to-end, combining reusable layout components with dynamic client-side JavaScript logic.
points: Designed responsive UI layouts across 8+ pages using Bootstrap 5 and an 8px spatial grid.
Built dynamic DOM rendering for recipe kits, dietary filters, and nutrition details from JSON data.
Implemented interactive shopping cart state and checkout validations with localStorage persistence.
Created an interactive order tracking timeline to simulate a complete customer journey.

result.title: The Result
result.paragraph: Successfully delivered and presented a high-fidelity, interactive prototype at Sisters of Code, providing a seamless browsing and ordering experience with pure client-side technologies.

title: Sentiment Analysis on Product Reviews
subtitle: Impact of Preprocessing Techniques on Machine Learning Models (Logistic Regression, Naive Bayes, KNN)
description: A Year 4 NLP project investigating how text preprocessing techniques, BoW, and N-grams affect sentiment classification performance across multiple ML models.
appPrompt: Explore the complete Jupyter notebooks, preprocessing pipelines, model training code, and evaluation metrics on GitHub.

images.title: NLP Pipeline & Machine Learning Architecture
images.caption: Text cleaning, tokenization, BoW & N-grams representation, multi-model training (Logistic Regression, Naive Bayes, KNN), and evaluation metrics

situation.title: The Situation
situation.paragraph: Product reviews contain valuable customer opinions, but analyzing a large number of reviews manually is time-consuming. Our Year 4 NLP project focused on using machine learning to automatically classify product reviews into positive, negative, or neutral sentiments.

task.title: The Task
task.paragraph: Our task was to investigate whether text preprocessing techniques affect sentiment classification performance and to compare three machine learning models: Logistic Regression, Naive Bayes, and KNN.

action.title: The Action
action.paragraph: We collected product review data and performed basic text preprocessing, including tokenization and stopword removal. We then represented the text using Bag-of-Words (BoW) and N-grams, trained the three models, and evaluated them using Accuracy, Precision, Recall, and F1 Score.

result.title: The Result
result.paragraph: We compared the performance of the models across the different preprocessing techniques and identified which combination produced better sentiment classification results. The project helped us understand how NLP preprocessing and machine learning models influence text classification performance.

title: OCR & Automated Tabular Data Cleaning
subtitle: Full-Stack PDF Extraction and Transform2Tidy Engine with FastAPI & Local OCR
description: A full-stack web application extracting tabular data from PDF/image documents with locally hosted OCR (Marker) and transforming wide messy tables into structured tidy datasets.
appPrompt: Explore the complete full-stack codebase, FastAPI backend, local Marker OCR setup, and Transform2Tidy pipelines on GitHub.

images.title: Full-Stack System Architecture & Logic Flow
images.caption: React client layer, FastAPI gateway, local GPU Marker OCR extraction, and LLM-assisted Transform2Tidy processing pipeline

situation.title: The Situation
situation.paragraph: Organizations frequently have valuable data trapped inside complex PDF documents and scanned images. Manually copying, cleaning, and reshaping messy tables into structured, analysis-ready formats is tedious and time-consuming.

task.title: The Task
task.paragraph: My goal was to build a full-stack application to automatically extract tabular data from PDFs and images using local open-source OCR models without paid external APIs, and transform them into clean datasets following Hadley Wickham’s Tidy Data principles.

action.title: The Action
action.paragraph: I conducted technical research and developed the pipeline from model evaluation to full-stack integration:
points: Conducted a literature review and benchmarked open-source OCR engines (Marker vs. MinerU) on a local GPU server with zero external API dependencies.
Built a FastAPI backend pipeline to handle document uploads, parse PDF/images into Markdown, and extract raw CSV tables.
Engineered the Transform2Tidy automated workflow to convert multi-header and wide tables into standardized tidy data formats.
Developed an interactive Web UI for document uploads, live table previews, in-place edits, and one-click tidy CSV exports.

result.title: The Result
result.paragraph: Delivered a working first-draft prototype for testing, successfully validating that local OCR models combined with LLM restructuring can eliminate recurring API costs and streamline messy document table transformation.
